tested:
── VMware ESXi (nested hypervisor) ─────────────────────────────────────────
No entry existed for "esxi"/"vmware" - the image (id 549b81d7.../da3ddd85...,
/netplex/images/qemu/vmware/esxi-6.0/virtioa.qcow2) silently fell through to
GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (256/512 MB, 1 vCPU, no min_ram_mb enforcement - same class
of bug already fixed once for "isrv" and "titanium" above). Live-repro'd
2026-07-18 with the exact runtime params qemu.py derives from the fallback
profile (-m 512 -smp 1 -cpu host, virtio disk): the VMware bootloader gets partway
through decompressing /s.v00 and HALTS with "Fatal error: 10 (Out of resources)" -
a textbook ESXi-under-provisioned-RAM crash, not a broken image (VMware's own
published minimum for ESXi 6.0 is 4 GB RAM / 2 cores; installer enforces it).
Re-tested at 4096 MB / 2 vCPU: the boot-loader stage completes cleanly (all
modules load, "Relocating modules and starting up the kernel..." reached) -
confirming RAM/vCPU were the fallback profile's defect and this fix resolves it.
NOTE: a separate "#GP Exception 13 in world 32768:bootstrap" purple-screen was
observed after the loader stage on THIS dev host regardless of RAM/cpu_model
(host, Penryn)/machine type (pc, q35) - that reproduces identically because this
dev box is itself a nested KVM guest (systemd-detect-virt=kvm), so booting ESXi
here is double-nested virtualization (L0 hw -> L1 this host -> L2 ESXi), a known
fragile combination for a guest that is itself a Type-1 hypervisor. That is a
test-host environment limitation, not a netplex code defect - not addressed here;
a bare-metal (single-nesting-level) netplex host is expected to clear it once the
RAM/vCPU floor below is in place. disk_bus stays virtio (unchanged) - the image is
already packaged virtioa.qcow2 and live-repro proved virtio storage IS readable by
this ESXi build's bootloader (it loaded every module fine over it); nic is set to
e1000 (stock ESXi ships no inbox virtio-net driver - matches the platform's own
generic-vm fallback NIC choice for exactly this reason).

settings.description: VMware ESXi 6.0 nested hypervisor - needs >=4 GB RAM to clear the boot loader (verified live: 512 MB halts with a boot-loader OOM before reaching the kernel).
settings.min_enforcement_msg: VMware ESXi requires minimum 4 GB RAM and 2 vCPUs (VMware's published minimum) - below this the boot loader halts with "Fatal error: 10 (Out of resources)" while decompressing the kernel image.
